pages.task: A load has an impedance of 3 + j4 Ω. What is its size?
pages.why: √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 Ω. You will meet this load again later, seen through a transformer.

pages.name: Volts follow turns
pages.text: Two windings share one core and one flux. On 440 V, the primary's 880 turns give 0.5 V per turn. So the secondary's 230 turns give 115 V. The volts follow the turns.

pages.name: A 24 V winding
pages.task: A primary of 880 turns sits on 440 V. A control circuit needs 24 V. How many turns does its secondary need?
pages.why: 440 ÷ 880 = 0.5 V per turn. 24 ÷ 0.5 = 48 turns. Check: 48 turns × 0.5 V = 24 V.

pages.name: The 440 V side
pages.task: A 440 V to 115 V transformer supplies 40 A on its 115 V side. What current does its 440 V side take?
pages.why: The volts step down by 440 ÷ 115 = 3.826. So the amps step up by the same. 40 ÷ 3.826 = 10.45 A. Check: 440 × 10.45 and 115 × 40 both come to about 4600 W.

pages.task: A 440 V, 60 Hz supply feeds a primary of 880 turns. The load changes from 10 Ω to 5 Ω, and the secondary current doubles from 11.5 A to 23 A. What is the peak flux now?
pages.why: Φm = 440 ÷ (4.44 × 60 × 880) = 1.88 mWb. The load is not in the rule, so the flux stays put. The primary's current rises from 3.01 A to 6.01 A. That cancels the extra ampere-turns.

pages.why: (880 ÷ 230)² = 14.64. So the 440 V side sees 2.5 × 14.64 = 36.6 Ω. Check: 115 V on 2.5 Ω draws 46 A. The primary takes 46 × 230 ÷ 880 = 12.02 A. And 440 ÷ 12.02 = 36.6 Ω.

pages.name: A step-up
pages.task: A step-up transformer has 200 turns on 115 V. Its secondary has 800 turns and feeds 2.3 A. What current does the primary take?
pages.why: 800 × 2.3 = 1840 ampere-turns. The primary must cancel them, so it takes 1840 ÷ 200 = 9.2 A. Check the power. The secondary gives 115 × 800 ÷ 200 = 460 V. 460 × 2.3 and 115 × 9.2 both come to 1058 W.
